charts.title: 01_severe_sbp_hr_overlay
charts.caption: Severe arm over 72 h: the extraction's systolic-pressure and heart-rate milestones lag the engine by ~11 h (SBP<100 at 37.5 h vs 26.6 h; HR>90 at 37.6 h vs 26.8 h). Dotted lines mark the SBP<100 and HR>90 thresholds. This is the systolic half of the picture; on the MAP<65 shock threshold the order flips (see the study-05 milestone dumbbell).

charts.title: 03_severe_9panel_engine_vs_sbml
charts.caption: Severe arm, all 9 observables, engine vs SBML extraction over 72 h. Inflammation (tissue integrity, blood pathogen) overlaps bit-for-bit; every divergence is in the hemodynamic layer. Dotted lines mark the SBP<100 / MAP<65 / HR>90 thresholds — both arms cross MAP<65 within 72 h, the extraction (steel blue) first.

charts.title: 04_severe_mechanism_co_svr
charts.caption: Over 72 h both arms cross the MAP<65 shock threshold (extraction at 54.1 h to MAP 58, engine at 69.3 h to MAP 64) by different routes: the engine declines via cardiac-output failure with near-constant SVR (hypodynamic/low-output), while the extraction holds output and swings SVR — vasoconstriction then sympathetic-fatigue vasodilation (hyperdynamic/warm), reaching shock ~15 h earlier. The extraction's single AIR→sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor response the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted.

charts.title: 05_severe_phase_portrait_co_svr
charts.caption: Severe sepsis (severity 3) plotted as a path in cardiac-output x vascular-resistance space rather than as two separate time series. Dots mark 6-hour intervals; the square is the shared healthy baseline (t=0), the stars are the 72 h endpoints, and grey dashes are iso-MAP contours (MAP = 17.34 x CO x SVR — a relation that holds to <0.5% in BOTH arms with the same constant). Both arms begin at the same point and finish below the MAP<65 shock contour (engine ~64 vs extraction ~58 mmHg — both now across the <65 threshold by 72 h, the extraction ~15 h earlier), but by orthogonal routes: the real BioGears engine slides LEFT — cardiac output fails 5.8->4.0 L/min while SVR stays flat (cold, low-output decline) — whereas the SBML extraction slides DOWN — it holds/rebuilds output and lets SVR swing up then fall to 0.60 (warm, vasodilatory decline). The orthogonality is the finding: the extraction's single AIR->sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor axis that the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted, so the two cross into MAP<65 shock by physiologically different routes. This is the geometric view of studies 03/05.
